name: Brow lift (surgical)
lead: A surgical brow lift, also called a forehead lift, browlift or browplasty, is a cosmetic operation that raises a low or drooping eyebrow and softens horizontal forehead lines. It is also used when a heavy brow obstructs the upper visual field.[1] By moving the brow higher, it opens the space between brow and lid, which people seek to look more alert, less tired and younger around the eyes. Techniques include endoscopic, coronal, hairline (pretrichial), temporal, direct, mid-forehead and transblepharoplasty approaches.[1]

In looksmaxxing communities it is classed as 'hardmaxxing' (surgical and procedural enhancement). Forum members discuss it mainly as part of the upper-third and eye-area toolkit, often alongside blepharoplasty, and often as one item in multi-procedure trips abroad.[2][3] Proponents describe a higher brow position and a more open eye area as attractive; the published literature on brow lifts concerns aging, ptosis and patient satisfaction, and a small body of work relates brow height and shape to aesthetic ideals in women.[4][5]

Published research includes retrospective case series of endoscopic and direct brow lifts, a photographic study of brow position in younger and older women, and studies of non-surgical alternatives such as botulinum toxin and energy-based devices.[6][7][4][10][11] Complications are described in the literature as uncommon but include numbness, hair loss at incision sites, asymmetry and scarring, depending on technique.[1][6][7]

paras: The procedure repositions the eyebrow and surrounding forehead soft tissue upward. Wikipedia describes it as treating a drooping brow that can impair vision and as softening deep forehead lines.[1] The brow tissue is released and then fixed in a higher position using sutures, screws, tissue adhesives or absorbable implants, depending on the surgeon and technique.[1][6]

Surgeons distinguish a brow lift from upper-eyelid surgery. Blepharoplasty removes excess lid skin, whereas a brow lift moves the brow itself, and the two are frequently combined; in one large endoscopic series, upper blepharoplasty was performed alongside the brow lift in 214 of 538 patients.[6]

Endoscopic brow lifts use several short incisions behind the hairline and a camera-guided instrument; Wikipedia describes about three to five incisions of roughly 3/8 inch each, with the surgeon working from a monitor. It is described as the most commonly used method.[1] The coronal technique uses a long incision across the scalp and was popular in the 1980s and 1990s but is described as less favored today.[1] Other approaches include the hairline (pretrichial) lift, the temporal lift aimed at the outer brow, the internal lift performed through an upper-eyelid incision, the mid-forehead lift, and the direct brow lift, in which a strip of skin is removed just above the brow.[1]

Fixation methods are a topic in their own right. Wikipedia notes that absorbable Endotine implants may shift with small movements before healing is complete and may not hold very thick forehead tissue or heavy brows.[1] A personal series of 538 patients compared fixation techniques for endoscopic brow lifts (see Clinical studies).[6] Botulinum toxin is sometimes added after surgery to extend results.[1]

A 2009 study in Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery photographed two groups of women, aged 20 to 30 (36 women) and 50 to 60 (34 women), excluding anyone with prior surgery, plucked brows or toxin treatment. It measured brow height from a line between the inner eye corners. In the younger group the brow sat about 15.7 mm above the inner corner, 19.8 mm above the pupil and 21.3 mm above the outer corner, with the outer brow significantly higher than the middle. Older women's brows measured about 19.1, 22.4 and 22.4 mm at the same points, higher at all three, significantly so at the inner and middle brow.[4] In this sample the older women's brows were measured as higher, not lower, than the younger women's.[4]

A 1996 study in the same journal asked eleven cosmetic surgeons and nine cosmetologists to rate computer-altered images in which only brow height and shape changed, then examined 100 pre- and 100 post-operative photographs from 16 frequently cited brow lift papers. Both groups preferred medial brows at or below the supraorbital rim and an apex that slanted laterally. After surgery in those photographs, the number of medial brows elevated above the rim rose significantly and lateral-apex brows did not increase significantly; the authors concluded that standard open and endoscopic lifts often produced brow height and shape that did not match these criteria.[5] Both studies concern female faces and specific ideals, and neither is a general statement about attractiveness.

Botulinum toxin injections can raise the outer brow by weakening muscles that pull it down; a 2000 prospective case series of 22 patients tested this directly, measuring brow elevation after injection directed at the brow depressors.[10] Wikipedia notes that many people choose injections repeated every four to six months instead of surgery, and that injections are sometimes used after surgery to extend results.[1] A Phase 4 trial registered as NCT01401803 evaluated Dysport for brow lifting in 24 participants.[16]

Energy devices have also been studied. A rater-blinded prospective cohort study in the Journal of the American Academy of Dermatology assessed ultrasound skin tightening for brow lift in the context of a full-face and neck treatment.[11] Registered trials have examined Sofwave (NCT04969380) and Matrix Pro (NCT06640998) for eyebrow lift, and a Zift device study (NCT03055819) was terminated.[18][19][17] A planned trial (NCT07879456) will examine thread-assisted brow suspension combined with upper blepharoplasty-assisted ligament release.[21]

According to Wikipedia, complications are described as rare and usually minor when performed by a trained surgeon. Numbness was most common after direct brow lifts, hair loss after endoscopic lifts, and hairline elevation or reduced scalp sensation after coronal lifts. Revision rates are described as highest after hairline brow lifts. In about 1% of endoscopic cases surgeons convert to the open method. Infection and bleeding are risks of any surgery.[1]

A retrospective review of direct brow lifts performed between 1989 and 2002 reported predictable results and high patient satisfaction, with scars seldom judged unacceptable when closure was careful, though they may be more noticeable in younger patients. Numbness of the forehead was described as a common but well-tolerated sequel.[7]

Brow lift surgery has also been reported to alter migraine symptoms in some patients when the corrugator muscle is resected, an observation that prompted anatomical research on headache trigger sites.[12]

On looksmax.org, brow lifts appear in forum posts about combined surgical trips. One member described flying to Antalya, Turkey for a package that included a brow lift among other facial procedures, with a stated cost of about US$15,000, and was asked how to find surgeons and to post before-and-after photos.[2] Other threads ask for feedback about lateral brow lifts and discuss botulinum toxin as a brow-raising measure.[13][14] Members also post about early recovery, with one asking whether a swollen, 'uncanny' look at 16 days after multiple procedures is normal.[15]

The brow sits within what forum members call the eye area or upper third, so brow lifts are usually discussed with canthoplasty, blepharoplasty and under-eye work rather than on their own.[2][15] Aesthetic surgery societies track the wider trend: the ISAPS 14-year analysis covers surgical and non-surgical aesthetic procedures worldwide, the context in which brow and eyelid procedures are offered.[22]

Human studies include a rater-blinded prospective cohort of ultrasound skin tightening that assessed brow lift as an outcome,[11] a prospective case series of botulinum toxin for temporal brow lift,[10] and surgical series of endoscopic and direct brow lifts.[6][7]

The endoscopic series by Jones and Grover (Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery, 2004) was a retrospective comparison of 538 consecutive patients over six years. Surgeons measured mid-pupil-to-brow distance before surgery and at follow-up. Fibrin glue fixation was used in 189 patients and polydioxanone sutures through bone tunnels in 349. Both groups gained about 6 mm of brow height at one month. At a mean of 9.4 months the fibrin glue group had relapsed from 5.93 mm to 3.79 mm, while the tunnel group held at about 6.2 mm. Blepharoplasty did not change long-term outcomes. Complications were few: one infection, two temporary alopecia cases and one reoperation for relapse in the glue group; four minor lateral port-scar revisions, three temporary temporal alopecia cases and one frontal-branch paresis that recovered by four months in the tunnel group.[6]

Registered trials include a Phase 4 trial of Dysport for brow lifting (NCT01401803, 24 participants),[16] a terminated trial of the Zift device for lifting facial tissue (NCT03055819),[17] trials of Sofwave and Matrix Pro energy devices for eyebrow lift (NCT04969380, NCT06640998),[18][19] a trial of non-ablative laser for direct brow lift scars (NCT02032641),[20] and a planned trial of thread-assisted brow suspension (NCT07879456).[21] A 2017 French article on forehead rejuvenation and a 2024 review of periorbital rejuvenation address the wider area.[23][24]

lore.intro: Brow lifts are discussed on looksmax.org mainly as one element of eye-area and upper-third surgery, often inside multi-procedure packages abroad.[2][13]

claims.claim: A higher or more lateral brow position improves facial attractiveness
claims.believers: Members seeking feedback on lateral brow lifts and combined eye surgery say a lifted brow opens the eye area and improves the look of the upper third.[13][2]
claims.experts: Surgical literature relates brow height and shape to aging and to ideals in women, and reports patient satisfaction with specific techniques; it does not establish a general attractiveness effect.[8][9][7]

claims.claim: Botulinum toxin can serve as a non-surgical brow lift
claims.believers: Forum threads discuss injecting around the brow to raise its tail as a lower-commitment alternative.[14]
claims.experts: A 2000 case series of 22 patients tested brow elevation after toxin injection,[10] and a Phase 4 trial has examined toxin for brow lifting.[16] Wikipedia notes injections are typically repeated every four to six months.[1]

claims.claim: Bundling many procedures abroad is a practical route to a large change
claims.believers: One poster described a single trip combining a brow lift with jaw, lip, cheek and dental work, citing a cost of about US$15,000.[2]
claims.experts: Published sources cited here do not evaluate multi-procedure medical travel. Surgical series report complications for individual brow lift techniques.[1][6]

claims.claim: Early swelling and an 'uncanny' look settle with time
claims.believers: A poster asked at 16 days after a brow lift and other procedures whether looking uncanny was normal, and others in forum recovery threads treat early swelling as expected.[15]
claims.experts: Surgical series report temporary effects such as numbness and short-lived hair loss that resolved within months in most cases.[6][7]

card.summary: Surgery that raises a drooping brow and opens the eye area; well-documented in the plastic surgery literature, popular in forum surgery packages.
card.aka: Forehead lift, browplasty, endoscopic brow lift
card.note: Surgical risks include numbness, hair loss at incisions, scarring and asymmetry.

quick.overview:
A surgical brow lift repositions the eyebrow and forehead tissue higher. It is used for drooping brows that crowd the eye and for forehead lines, and looksmaxxing forums treat it as part of eye-area hardmaxxing.

Techniques range from endoscopic and coronal lifts to direct and temporal lifts. Non-surgical options such as botulinum toxin and ultrasound devices are also studied.
quick.mechanism: The surgeon releases the brow tissue and fixes it in a higher position using incisions at the hairline, temple, brow or upper eyelid, depending on the technique.
quick.risks: Reported complications include numbness, hair loss, hairline elevation, scarring, asymmetry, infection and bleeding. Rates vary by technique and surgeon, and the literature describes serious complications as uncommon.

chain: Brow tissue is released and fixed higher
Brow sits further from the lid, opening the eye area
Eyes read as more open, alert and youthful; forehead lines soften
angle.text: A brow lift changes the resting height and sometimes the tail position of the eyebrow, which alters how much lid and eye is visible. People use it for a lifted, more open upper third and for smoother forehead skin, often combined with eyelid surgery.
